claims.text: An actively learned machine-learning interatomic potential can reproduce ab initio free energies for multicomponent high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid phases over 0.8–1.2 Tm.
The proposed framework can reduce computational cost by at least an order of magnitude relative to full ab initio molecular dynamics.
Uncertainty quantification can reliably identify when additional DFT sampling is required.
The proposed application system is equimolar NiCoFeCrMn in equilibrium solid and liquid configurations.
Dynamically adding DFT data for high-uncertainty configurations will correct deficient regions of the MLIP configuration space.
MLIP-generated configuration ensembles capture anharmonic vibrational modes.
MLIP-generated configuration ensembles capture electron–vibration coupling.
The representation of anharmonic vibrational modes and electron–vibration coupling has been validated against periodic DFT calculations.
Pinpointing uncertain configurations through active learning minimizes the number of DFT evaluations.
Targeted active-learning sampling ensures accurate reproduction of solid and liquid free-energy landscapes.
The reproduced free-energy landscapes retain all entropy components essential to fusion thermodynamics.
The proposed method will predict phase free-energy differences within approximately 5% of explicit AIMD benchmarks.
The proposed method will predict melting properties within approximately 5% of explicit AIMD benchmarks.
Prior elemental and binary studies have demonstrated explicit AIMD free-energy evaluations and TOR-TILD as relevant comparison methods.
The method is expected to be robust for multicomponent high-entropy alloys between 0.8 and 1.2 Tm.
Regimes with extreme anharmonicity may require additional validation or methodological adjustments.
